title: Climate, Peace and Security Fact Sheet: South Sudan (2025)
temporal_coverage: Climate, peace, and security conditions synthesized for the 2025 fact sheet.
methodology: SIPRI and partner authors synthesize climate trends, conflict dynamics, institutional context, and policy implications into a country fact sheet with recommended actions.
limitations: The official catalogue states April 2025 without a day, so publication_date preserves month precision; the concise synthesis does not replace review of its underlying sources.

title: Climate Security Risks in South Sudan: An Information Brief (2025)
temporal_coverage: Current climate-security risks and response priorities as assessed in 2025.
methodology: The information brief was jointly developed by UNDP, UNMISS, and the UN Resident Coordinator's Office to synthesize climate-related security risks and strategic interventions for South Sudan.
limitations: This is a short strategic brief rather than a reproducible dataset; its country-level framing can obscure variation among states, livelihood systems, and conflict settings.

title: Joining Forces for a Conflict-Sensitive Flood Response in South Sudan (2025)
geographic_coverage: South Sudan (national and selected flood-affected subnational locations)
temporal_coverage: Lessons from the 2024 flood response and preparedness priorities for the 2025 flood season.
methodology: The article distils a UN Community of Practice discussion and operational examples from UNMISS, OCHA, the UN Country Team, national authorities, and subnational flood taskforces.
limitations: The source is a practice-oriented UN news account, not an independent evaluation; selected operational examples cannot establish how consistently conflict sensitivity was applied nationwide.

title: South Sudan Country Climate and Development Report (2026)
temporal_coverage: Historical climate and development baselines with forward-looking climate and development analysis published in 2026.
methodology: The World Bank country diagnostic integrates climate information with macroeconomic, sectoral, institutional, and development analysis to identify climate-resilient development priorities.
limitations: A national diagnostic may mask subnational differences and depends on model assumptions and uneven underlying data availability; this record does not independently reproduce or verify those inputs.

title: First National Adaptation Plan for Climate Change Republic of South Sudan
organization: Government of the Republic of South Sudan and United Nations Development Programme (UNDP)
methodology: The national planning document organizes adaptation around three resilience pillars and nine priority sectors to guide policy and implementation from national to community level.
limitations: The plan records government priorities and intended actions rather than evaluated adaptation outcomes; implementation progress after its 2021-2025 planning horizon requires separate evidence.

title: South Sudan Second Nationally Determined Contribution
organization: Government of the Republic of South Sudan and United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change (UNFCCC)
temporal_coverage: National climate commitments and priorities submitted in 2021, principally oriented to 2030.
methodology: The government submission updates the national greenhouse-gas inventory and sets sectoral mitigation, adaptation, and implementation commitments under the Paris Agreement.
limitations: The date recorded is the UNFCCC submission date, 2021-09-21, not the portal file-publication timestamp; an NDC states commitments and assumptions rather than demonstrating achieved results.

title: South Sudan Flood Damage and Needs Assessment Study (2021)
organization: International Organization for Migration (IOM) Displacement Tracking Matrix (DTM)
geographic_coverage: Three flood-affected payams in South Sudan
temporal_coverage: Impacts of the June-December 2020 floods, with fieldwork from 2021-08-31 to 2021-10-14.
methodology: IOM field-validated the 2020 flood assessment using two quantitative tools, focus-group discussions, and key-informant interviews, consulting more than 1,131 people across three payams.
limitations: The official page states publication year 2021 without an exact month or day, so publication_date preserves year precision; purposive coverage of three payams is not nationally representative.

title: South Sudan UN Common Country Analysis (CCA)
organization: United Nations Resident Coordinator's Office in South Sudan
temporal_coverage: Multisector country context through late 2021, published on the UN portal in 2022.
methodology: The UN country analysis synthesizes political, conflict, humanitarian, socioeconomic, environmental, and institutional evidence to identify constraints to sustainable development.
limitations: The portal publication date, 2022-06-27, is used consistently, while the downloadable document is versioned 2021-12-24; underlying indicators have different reference periods and may have since changed.

title: INFORM South Sudan Country Risk Profile (2021)
temporal_coverage: INFORM 2021 risk profile, including trend displays for 2017-2021.
methodology: INFORM combines standardized indicators of hazard and exposure, vulnerability, and lack of coping capacity into a composite country risk index with peer and trend comparisons.
limitations: The profile identifies version 2021 rather than a dated publication, so publication_date records the stated version year; composite national scores compress indicator uncertainty and subnational disparities.

title: Climate change deepens gender inequality and violence in South Sudan: UNFPA study highlights urgent need for action
organization: United Nations Population Fund (UNFPA), Sudd Institute, and South Sudan National Bureau of Statistics
temporal_coverage: Study findings released in 2025 on current climate-related gender and violence risks.
methodology: The UN story summarizes a vulnerability study conducted by UNFPA with the Sudd Institute and National Bureau of Statistics in three high-exposure locations, with findings validated in a stakeholder workshop.
limitations: This is a summary rather than the full study methodology; purposive selection of three highly exposed locations and condensed reporting limit national generalization.

title: South Sudan Event Tracking Report 73: Flood Displacements (1-31 December 2024)
organization: International Organization for Migration (IOM) Displacement Tracking Matrix (DTM)
temporal_coverage: Flood-related displacement events recorded from 2024-12-01 to 2024-12-31.
methodology: IOM DTM enumerators used event tracking to document disaster-related displacement during December 2024 and record affected people's reported priority needs.
limitations: Event tracking is a rapid, period-specific account rather than a complete displacement stock; the 2025-02-10 publication date follows the December 2024 observation period.

title: South Sudan Climatology (ERA5)
organization: World Bank Climate Change Knowledge Portal
temporal_coverage: ERA5 climatology for 1991-2020 and historical daily data for 1950-2023.
methodology: The World Bank Climate Change Knowledge Portal presents ERA5 reanalysis-derived South Sudan climatology for 1991-2020 and historical daily data for 1950-2023 at 0.25-degree resolution.
limitations: ERA5 is model-based reanalysis rather than direct station observation, and national summaries can mask subnational variation. This living page can change and has no fixed publication date; publication_date remains null with basis not-stated.
